clue.text: Song and dance about reflective Rashford's transfer tweet?

indicators.note: the dance goes around the other piece, so it is placed about it

parts.note: the haka is the Maori war dance performed by New Zealand's rugby team

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the tweet is read backwards

parts.note: a footballer leaving Manchester United might tweet TA TA MAN U, goodbye to the club

explanation.surface: A footballer's farewell message on leaving his club is turned into a big song-and-dance affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcus Rashford plays for Manchester United, Man U; 'ta ta' is British for goodbye. 'Reflective' turns the tweet back to front, and 'about' wraps the dance round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hakuna Matata is the well-known number from Disney's The Lion King, so it is a song.

clue.text: Famous Vietnamese hospital: I am impatient and I am an in-patient

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
och is the Scottish exclamation of impatience, as if the speaker were saying it
I'm is the contraction of I am
someone in hospital is IN H, H being hospital again

explanation.surface: A patient in a Vietnamese hospital grumbles about waiting while being treated there.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is built as speech: OCH is a Scots cry of impatience, and 'I am an in-patient' becomes I'M IN H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho Chi Minh led North Vietnam and is the country's most celebrated revolutionary figure.

clue.text: Bizarrely attractive, Frankfort's heart — here!

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here the fifth of nine

parts.note: Frankfort is the capital of Kentucky, so 'here' from its viewpoint means IN KY, KY being Kentucky's abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone calls a place in Frankfort, perhaps the German one, oddly appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Frankfort is not Frankfurt in Germany but the capital of the US state of Kentucky, so 'here' means in Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinky describes tastes that are unconventional, especially in a sexual way, so strangely alluring.

clue.text: A little non-U, charmless scruff

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone ill-bred and lacking charm is a bit of a scruff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scruff' looks like a scruffy person; here it is the nape of the neck. Non-U is British for not upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: The nucha is the anatomical term for the nape, the back of the neck, also called the scruff.

clue.text: Young woman's clothed fashionably in red garment

indicators.note: the young woman is clothed in the other letters, so they go inside her

parts.note: a miss is a young woman; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: the words in red are styled anew, their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl is dressed stylishly in red clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like the insertion signal, but it is part of the fodder 'fashionably' rearranges; 'clothed' is what puts the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A minidress is a short dress, so a garment.

clue.text: Sailor's newspaper leading on a Spanish seaport

indicators.note: the newspaper goes first, in front of the following words

parts.note: a tar is a sailor; the 's means has
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor's paper is the top story in a Spanish port.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragona is a port city on the Mediterranean coast of Catalonia in Spain.

clue.text: Still worked up about large student set

indicators.note: the reversed word goes about the two letters
in a down clue the word for still is worked upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'yet more'
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
L is a learner, from the L-plate of a student driver

explanation.surface: A student gets worked up all over again about something large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked up' turns YET into TEY, which goes around LL. The L-plate marks a British learner driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A telly is British slang for a television, and a TV set is a set.

clue.text: Bows rot!

definitions.meaning: the bows used to play a fiddle

explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle's bow is its stick, and as an exclamation fiddlesticks dismisses nonsense, like rot.

clue.text: Apparently ready for release of empire's supreme ruler

definitions.meaning: a finished film is said to be 'in the can', so the answer read as two words says ready for release
The adjective for the Inca, supreme ruler of the Andean empire

explanation.definitionFit: A completed film is in the can, and the Inca was emperor of the Peruvian empire, so Incan describes him.

clue.text: Singers being heard in court, one delayed

indicators.note: the one is held back and comes later in the word
the trial phrase sits inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a case being heard is on trial
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Several singers are giving evidence in court, one of them arriving late.
explanation.walkthrough: ON TRIAL inside CT gives CONTRIALT; 'delayed' moves its I to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Contralti is the Italian plural of contralto, the lowest female singing voice.

clue.text: Fine to wear, when cooking, is it apt, chef?

definitions.text: Fine to wear, when cooking, is it apt, chef?

indicators.note: the anagram wears the letter, so it goes inside
the words are cooked up, their letters rearranged

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A chef is asked whether a hat is suitable to wear while cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When cooking' rearranges IS IT APT CHEF; 'to wear' puts F inside. The whole clue also defines: the saying 'if the cap fits, wear it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'if the cap fits, wear it' means accept a criticism that suits you, so asking if the hat suits.

clue.text: 14 heading over to assist farm girl

indicators.note: the word is headed back over, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: 14 is SHEDLOADS, a great deal, which here means myriad
to aid is to assist

explanation.surface: A large number of people go over to help a girl on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 14 (SHEDLOADS) gives MYRIAD; 'heading over' reverses it to DAIRYM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid is a woman who works in a dairy, milking and making butter on a farm.

clue.text: Inordinately easy start to Toughie? Till now!

indicators.note: out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A solver says that so far this Toughie has been unusually easy.
explanation.definitionFit: As yet means up to the present time, so till now.

clue.text: Composer's one piece of work covered by Ireland retrospective

indicators.note: looking back, so the whole is read in reverse
the one and the work go inside the name for Ireland, which covers them

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
I is the Roman numeral one
a task is a piece of work

explanation.surface: A composer's single work features in an Irish retrospective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered by' puts the work inside before 'retrospective' turns the whole thing round, so the answer reads backwards. 'Composer's' is composer is.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was the French composer of the Gymnopédies.

clue.text: What unfortunate lorry-drivers may do a great deal

definitions.meaning: an unlucky lorry driver may ..., spilling the cargo onto the road
British slang for a large amount

explanation.definitionFit: Shedloads is informal British for a huge quantity, and lorries can lose their cargo on the motorway.

clue.text: Daily, the suspect's admitted on charge

indicators.note: the suspect has the other letters admitted inside it
suspect means doubtful or dodgy, so the letters of the word the are rearranged

parts.note: the on side in cricket is also called the leg side
a rap is a criminal charge

explanation.surface: In a newspaper report, the suspect confesses to a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' rearranges a word of the clue and 'admitted' takes the rest inside. In cricket the on side is also called the leg side. 'Suspect's' is suspect has.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Telegraph is a British newspaper, so a daily.

clue.text: Nothing pleasant, alone in pen?

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Nothing is nice about being on your own in a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' is not a writing pen but a penitentiary; on ice is slang for being locked away, and the question mark flags the loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: On ice is slang for imprisoned or kept in solitary, which fits a lone prisoner in the penitentiary.

clue.text: Happy — as Gagarin's medium or the Husband of Rhum?

definitions.meaning: in good spirits means cheerful, so happy

definitions.text: as Gagarin's medium or the Husband of Rhum?
definitions.meaning: AGAR, a growing medium, sits inside GIN in GAGARIN, and H, for husband, sits inside RUM in RHUM: both

explanation.walkthrough: Gagarin was the first man in space and Rhum is a Scottish island, but here both are just words with something inside a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in high spirits means cheerful; literally, agar and H are inside the spirits gin and rum.

clue.text: Lake resort near Spain — it's lovely visiting

indicators.note: the sigh visits, going inside the other word

parts.note: to can mean near, as in close to
ah is the sigh someone gives at something lovely
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone praises a lakeside resort close to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe, on the California–Nevada border, is a well-known holiday and ski resort.

clue.text: Look at that set of numbers, each describing ratings that have gone down?

definitions.text: describing ratings that have gone down?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
stats, short for statistics, are a set of numbers

explanation.surface: An analyst looks at the figures for something whose ratings have fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratings' suggests TV audience figures; in the Navy ratings are ordinary sailors, here gone down with their ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors lost at sea have drowned when their ship went down.

clue.text: Is out of food, hot and cold

indicators.note: the letter is out of the food, so removed from it

parts.note: chilli is a hot food
read as I's, the letter I is

explanation.surface: Someone has run out of food, both hot and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is out of' reads as 'I is out of', so I comes out of CHILLI.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a feeling of coldness, and chill as an adjective means cold.

clue.text: Enjoys life on rented eyot

parts.note: to be is to exist, so is means lives
let means rented out

explanation.surface: Someone has a fine time living on an island they lease.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small island in a river, especially the Thames, so an islet.

clue.text: My word for doggie barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A dog lover exclaims at the yapping of a pet dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' is the noise the doggie makes, but it is British slang for crazy, so the letters of FOR DOGGIE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Good grief and my word are both exclamations of surprise.

clue.text: On time for public viewing

parts.note: over can mean on, as in on top of

explanation.surface: A show is ready on schedule for the public to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means openly done, not hidden, so out in the open.

clue.text: 22! Someone finishing off tender curry-house meat

parts.note: 22 is GOOD GRIEF, an exclamation also expressed as gosh

indicators.note: the finisher is taken off the word tender

parts.note: someone who finishes is an ender

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone polishing off the tender meat in an Indian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ENDER from TENDER leaves only T. 'Tender' looks like part of the definition but is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosht is the Hindi and Urdu word for meat, usually lamb or mutton, found on Indian menus.

clue.text: Conscious of No 1 principality to the west receiving first 25% of passengers

indicators.note: the reversed country receives the first of the four letters of the passengers' word, a quarter of it
in an across clue westward is leftward, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: Wales is often called the Principality
the fares are a cab's passengers

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of himself first as a principality takes in passengers from the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the west' reverses the country; passengers in a cab pay fares. 'Receiving first 25% of' moves the first of four letters into the reversed country. Number one means oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one is oneself, so conscious of number one is aware of oneself.

clue.text: Churchman, satirist and flier

definitions.meaning: Jonathan ... was Dean of St Patrick's Cathedral in Dublin
... wrote Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal

explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift was both an Anglican dean and a satirist, and the swift is a bird famed for its flight.

clue.text: An inflammation, but which one? Let's move on

parts.note: the suffix -itis marks an inflammation, as in tonsillitis
what can mean which, as in 'what one?'
the one asked about is the inflammation, again -itis

explanation.surface: A patient told of an inflammation asks which one, and the doctor shrugs it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' is a link word. The question 'which one?' becomes WHAT ITIS.
explanation.definitionFit: It is what it is is a shrugging idiom accepting things that cannot be changed, so time to move on.
